newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - April 24.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on April 24. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Jakarta governor Surjadi has reiterated the government's stance of not allowing street campaigns by the three political parties contesting the general elections on May 29. The official campaign, in which the ruling Golkar, the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) and the Christian-Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) will participate, starts on April 27 and last until May 24.

The Jakarta Stock Exchange (JSX) has suspended four stock broking houses for failing to deliver Bank Pikko shares to their buyers within nine days of transactions. The Capital Market Supervisory Agency has earlier questioned three JSX directors over trade in Bank Pikko shares on April 8 when the bank's shares soared 207 percent to 4,000 rupiah in four hours before being suspended.
President Suharto has denied that the government's project to convert one million hectares of peat moss land in central Kalimantan into rice producing areas was a haphazard decision.
